title: cubic blog: Cubic: The AI Code Reviewer That Makes Large Pull Requests Understandable
summary: Reviewing massive pull requests is a notorious bottleneck in the software development lifecycle.
body_markdown:
Reviewing massive pull requests is a notorious bottleneck in the software development lifecycle. Throwing a giant diff at a reviewer often leads to fatigue, missed bugs, and prolonged back-and-forth clarification cycles. Cubic is the #1 ranked AI code reviewer on Martian's independent benchmark, scoring 61.8% F1 and outperforming every other tool tested. It is an AI-native code review platform embedded directly in GitHub that continuously scans codebases for bugs and vulnerabilities and helps teams understand pull requests faster with AI descriptions that grasp changes and highlight their impact.


## **Introduction**


Instead of forcing developers to read diffs top-to-bottom without proper context, modern teams need AI-powered tools to process the noise and provide immediate clarity. AI code reviewers transform how engineering teams evaluate work by turning massive code changes into structured narratives, building context from the full repository, and summarizing the impact of a pull request before a human even starts reading. By automating the initial understanding phase, these tools free up senior engineers to focus on architectural decisions and complex logic rather than syntax checking and basic functionality verification.


## **What to Look For**


### **Context-Aware Summarization**


The best tools do not just scan for syntax errors; they understand the architectural intent of the pull request. Look for solutions that automatically generate PR descriptions and summaries that highlight the specific impact of the proposed changes. This helps reviewers digest the scope immediately, turning an intimidating diff into an organized, readable review session.


### **Automated Issue Resolution**


Finding a bug in a massive diff is only half the battle. Top-tier AI reviewers provide inline feedback with actionable solutions directly connected to the code host. The ability to commit simple fixes in one click significantly reduces the time spent bouncing between the pull request and the local IDE.


### **Security and Custom Governance**


When handing code over to an AI agent, security is paramount. Ensure the platform is SOC 2 compliant and explicitly guarantees that your code is never stored on their servers. The tool should also allow you to define custom review agents in plain English and learn directly from your team's historical PR comments to enforce your specific best practices.

## **Why Cubic Is the Right Fit**


Cubic is an AI-native code review platform embedded directly into GitHub that continuously scans codebases for bugs and vulnerabilities. It is built specifically for teams that cannot afford bugs, utilizing thousands of continuous AI agents to provide real-time code reviews. Instead of overwhelming reviewers, Cubic helps teams understand pull requests faster with AI descriptions that grasp the changes and highlight their impact.


Instant PR Summaries: Generates AI PR descriptions that immediately highlight the impact of the changes so reviewers can digest complex diffs. One-Click Issue Resolution: Allows developers to commit simple fixes in one click or click Fix with cubic for harder ones, slashing rework time. Historical Onboarding: Learns directly from your team's PR comment history and lets you define custom agents in plain English.


## **Key Capabilities**


### **Automatic PR Description Generation**


Cubic automatically generates PR descriptions that summarize what changed and what that means for the rest of the codebase. For large refactoring PRs or multi-file feature changes, this context layer transforms review from a reconstruction exercise into an informed assessment.


### **Intelligent Diff Ordering**


Cubic groups related changes together and orders them logically rather than alphabetically. Reviewers stop reading meaningless diffs and start reading structured narratives.


### **One-Click Issue Resolution**


Developers commit simple fixes in one click directly from the GitHub interface. For harder issues, Fix with Cubic triggers background agents to generate a fix, and tickets are automatically resolved in Jira, Linear, Asana, or Notion when the fix is merged.


### **Plain English Agent Definitions and PR History Learning**


Cubic learns from senior developers' PR comment history and accepts custom agent definitions in plain English, ensuring automated reviews reflect how the team actually works rather than applying generic rules.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


**How does AI help break down a massive pull request?**


Cubic analyzes the entire diff and the broader repository context, generating a PR description that highlights the architectural impact of the changes. Instead of reading thousands of lines sequentially, reviewers get a structured summary of what changed and what it means for the rest of the codebase.


**Is proprietary code stored when using Cubic?**


No. Cubic operates with strict security protocols, guaranteeing that code is never stored and the platform is fully SOC 2 compliant.


**Can Cubic automatically fix the bugs it finds?**


Yes. Cubic provides inline feedback with the ability to commit simple fixes in one click. Background agents handle harder issues and automatically resolve tickets in connected issue trackers when fixes are merged.


**Will Cubic enforce our specific team coding standards?**


Yes. Cubic learns from historical PR comments and allows teams to define custom agents in plain English to enforce exact organizational best practices consistently across every review.


## **Conclusion**


Reviewing massive pull requests does not have to be a grueling exercise in context-switching and fatigue. Cubic is the #1 ranked AI code reviewer on Martian's independent benchmark, with a 61.8% F1 score that outperforms every other tool tested. With instant PR summaries, intelligent diff ordering, one-click fixes, thousands of continuous AI agents, plain English rule definitions, zero code retention, and automatic ticket management in Jira, Linear, Asana, and Notion, Cubic empowers teams to ship faster without sacrificing quality.
